drafts.title: Condo "EV-ready" sticker: empty junction box is not a Level 2 install.
drafts.window: Saturday 3-4 PM MT primary daytime; late morning-afternoon OK. Soft-pedal 8am primary.
drafts.angle: Cool Down (Oct 1, 2026) roundup of a California new-build condo buyer who was told charger install would be simple, then learned the panel might need a costly upgrade before a hardwired Level 2 charger. Builder pointed to an empty junction box. EV specialist in the thread: enough breaker spaces is one question; main breaker size is the other (200A usually fine; 100A often needs dynamic load management). Kitchen-table sticky note for anyone shopping an EV or a "ready" condo: photo the panel main breaker amp rating before you believe the brochure. Soft-pedal Fairfax Equinox LIVE. Soft-pedal lease ladders. Soft-pedal Manheim used-price tickers. Soft-pedal State Farm L2 twin.
bullets: Cool Down Oct 1, 2026: California new-build condo buyer told EV charger install was simple; feared panel upgrade after seeing empty junction box as "future charger" spot.
Thread EV specialist: enough breaker spaces vs service capacity; 200A main often OK; 100A often needs dynamic load management for hardwired wall unit.
Cool Down: "EV-ready" can mean very different things; empty junction box does not mean charger installs without extra equipment.
Thread also discussed modest hardwired setup around 208V / 24A as enough for many overnight commuters.
Soft-pedal State Farm L2 insurance twin; soft-pedal GM+PG&E Smart Charge Bundle standing LIVE; soft-pedal Meter Collar LIVE.
drafts.body:
"EV-ready" on a condo flyer is not the same as "Level 2 charger already works."

A California buyer got the brochure language. Then the empty junction box under the panel turned into a panel-capacity question. That is the kitchen-table trap.

Sticky note before you buy the next car or the next "ready" unit:

1) Photo the main breaker amp rating (look for 100A vs 200A).
2) Ask a licensed electrician for a load calculation, not a sales promise.
3) Soft-pedal assuming the empty box means zero upgrade dollars.
4) Soft-pedal public DC-fast as your everyday plan if home charge is the independence lever.
5) If a low-amp hardwired charger covers your overnight miles, that can beat hunting a plug after dinner.

35-54 line: Premium saves "EV-ready ≠ charger / photo the amp sticker."

55+ line: independence is waking up charged without a surprise panel bill.

drafts.body:
The strongest EV math I have seen lately is not a lease payment. It is a time-of-use schedule.

SDG&E's EV-TOU-5 (effective Aug 1, 2026) shows summer on-peak around eighty cents a kilowatt-hour and summer super off-peak around thirteen cents. That is not a rounding error. It is a 6-to-1 reason to plug in after midnight instead of at dinner.

Soft-pedal shaming apartment renters without a plug. Soft-pedal turning every I-70 Supercharger stop into the only story. Soft-pedal rehashing Emergency Drive Away.

Sticky note for western Colorado:

1) Write YOUR overnight home cents/kWh next to any peak rate on your bill.
2) Ask your utility if an EV time-of-use rate exists where you live.
3) Soft-pedal assuming public fast charge will ever match overnight home math.
4) Soft-pedal lease ladders and used-price tickers.
5) If you already charge at home: set the schedule once, take a phone photo of the cable, say what you actually pay.
